title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator for cyclotomic KLR algebras
statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let $E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\,\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$
(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\,\mathrm{Id}.$$
Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift conventions).

references.title: Seok-Jin Kang and Masaki Kashiwara, Categorification of Highest Weight Modules via Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier Algebras, arXiv:1102.4677v4
references.locator: Section 5.1-5.2: Theorem 5.2 with the two cases and the commutative diagrams (5.3)-(5.6), Proposition 5.3, Lemmas 5.4-5.5 and the final triangular isomorphism completing the proof.

references.title: Raphael Rouquier, 2-Kac-Moody Algebras, arXiv:0812.5023v3
references.locator: Section 4.1.3 (the sl_2 categorification axiom, quoted in the source as [15, Section 4.1.3], and Rouquier's Definition 5.1 of a 2-representation) and Section 5.1.

axiom_use: None: the exact-sequence and snake-lemma argument is choice-free.
